turns.prompt: Make a workflow that greets someone and then asks me to approve.
turns.finalText:
I'd save this as `.sous/workflows/greet-approve.js`. It follows the pattern of the existing `hello` and `review` workflows.

```js
export const meta = {
  name: "greet-approve",
  description: "Greet someone, then stop for a person to approve",
  inputs: { name: { type: "string", description: "Who to greet", required: true } },
  place: "none",
}

const greeted = await breakpoint(
  "Approve the greeting",
  () => js("return `hello ${input.name}`", { name: args.name }, { label: "greet" }),
  { show: (step) => step.result },
)
return { greeting: greeted.result }
```

The `greet` step builds the greeting. A `breakpoint` then shows it to you and waits until you approve. Breakpoints are always for people, so an agent can't approve it for you.

Should I save it and run `sous check greet-approve --name x --dry-run`? After that you'd need to approve the workflow text, either by telling me yes or by typing `sous workflows approve greet-approve`, before I can start it.

turns.prompt: Yes, save it and run it for Ada.
turns.finalText:
I saved `greet-approve`, it passed `sous check`, and I started it for Ada as run `mwuz449w-g322wf`. The run is now waiting for you at the breakpoint.

> **Breakpoint: Approve the greeting**
>
> hello Ada
>
> Reply approve, stop, or send back with a note.

Please tell me:
- **approve**: I'll approve it and the run will finish with `{ greeting: "hello Ada" }`.
- **send back**: give me a note and I'll pass it on.
- **stop**: I'll stop the run.

I haven't answered the breakpoint myself, because only you can answer it. The run will wait as long as it takes. You can also answer from your own terminal with `sous approve mwuz449w-g322wf--1`.

The workflow file is at `.sous/workflows/greet-approve.js`. It isn't committed to git.
